issues.description: Function teleport_s has inconsistent parameter ordering across artifacts. The problem statement (problem_statement.md) and the reference solution (solution_repository/msd.py) define the function as: teleport_s(circ: stim.Circuit, data_qubit: int, injection_qubit: int, p = 0.0) -> int (data_qubit first, injection_qubit second). The template stub (template_repository/msd.py) declares the signature with the parameters reversed: teleport_s(circ: stim.Circuit, injection_qubit: int, data_qubit: int, p = 0.0) -> int. This mismatch (signature vs. specification/solution) will confuse students about which argument corresponds to the data qubit vs. the injection qubit and can cause incorrect implementations or calls. Note: the template's docstring describes the parameters in the order (circ, data_qubit, injection_qubit) which matches the problem statement, increasing the likelihood of confusion because the documented order does not match the stub's actual parameter order.
issues.suggestedFix: Edit the template stub to match the problem statement and solution parameter order. Change the template signature to: def teleport_s(circ: stim.Circuit, data_qubit: int, injection_qubit: int, p: float = 0.0) -> int. Ensure the template docstring and any in-file references reflect the same ordering so students implement and call the function consistently.
